rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer A feels more like a real startup site. It shows the Fernwick brand, and its invoice card (with an UNPAID badge, client, due date, amount and 'Reminder sent today') is clearly specific to the product. Its weak point is the gradient 'Reminder sent today' bar, which looks a lot like the primary button and competes with it a little. Answer B is clean with clear hierarchy, but it never shows the brand name, and its illustration is generic and looks unfinished: a sketchy bell icon and a placeholder document. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B looks more like a real startup site: it has a brand mark, a stronger two-line headline, and an invoice card with a client, due date, amount and an UNPAID badge, so it clearly belongs to an invoice-reminder tool. Its weak spot is the solid gradient 'Reminder sent today' bar in the mockup, which looks like a second primary button. B's grey body text is also a little light. A is clean and has a clear hierarchy, but its visual is generic and sparse, with an odd bell icon, and the page feels unfinished because there is no branding.
